- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines sharply (e.g., >-3% over 3 days), model underreacts; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast tail.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is weak or neutral; apply 3–7% downward adjustment to first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10-day moving average is > 80% of 30-day forecast, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with historical volatility.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.17 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overpredict; apply 3–8% downward correction to forecast tail.
- If true outcome drops below 70% of 30-day forecast mean within 5 days, model often fails to recognize trend reversal; adjust forecast downward by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
